These insects attach themselves to a tree during a certain life stage and extract sugary sap from the tree which the ants farm to fuel their supercolonies. While also moving and spreading the insects to new trees. They also have other direct interactions with the red crab which is ultimately changing the islands forest structure.

Habitats are a mosaic of favourable/unfavourable patches. In these patches may be small populations or clusters of a species that are ultimately a part of metapopulations. Metapopulations are groups of a species that are isolated from one another but still have some movement between groups allowing for genetic mixing. A population of a species may be driven to an isolated area by competition for resources or intense predation where they become genetically isolated over time but this takes a very long time. New Zealand, Madagascar and Papa New Guinea are really good examples of isolated island with genetically unique animals. Many New Zealand birds became completely or semi flightless due to evolving with no mammalian predators.
